//Cache: The cache is always on in-process. Redis is the shared second tier, and Enabled is
the only switch: with it off each server remembers on its own, which is correct and
slightly wasteful behind a load balancer. Nothing that reads the cache names Redis,
so turning it off leaves an app that still works with a colder cache.

The API refuses to start with Enabled true and no connection string, rather than
quietly falling back: somebody who switched it on meant it.
KeyPrefix keeps two environments off each other's keys when they share one Redis.
Staging and production can hold the same tenant ids after a restored dump, so an
unprefixed key is a cross-environment read rather than a mix-up.
//Storage: Where patient files are kept, and the setting that decides whether the API can run
on more than one server. Local writes to the machine the request happened to land
on, so a file uploaded through one instance cannot be opened through another — the
symptom is a document that is there for some staff and missing for others.
Local is the default because it needs nothing provisioned and a clone of this
repository has to work. It is the right answer for a single-server practice.
Provider: S3 covers anything speaking the S3 protocol — AWS, Cloudflare R2, MinIO,
Supabase Storage. Set ServiceUrl for all but AWS, where Region picks the endpoint.
ForcePathStyle true for MinIO and most self-hosted gateways.

Better still, leave both empty on AWS: the SDK then uses the instance role or pod
identity, which rotates on its own and is never written down.
The key format is the same for both stores, so a practice on local disk is moved by
